newsitem.title: FRANCE: France and Spain say Zaire force still needed.
newsitem.headline: France and Spain say Zaire force still needed.

text.p: France and Spain said on Monday they still wanted a multinational force sent to Zaire even though hundreds of thousands of refugees have partly defused the crisis by trekking home to Rwanda.

"It's true that the situation is fluid and that this force will have to adapt its operational capacity, but for the moment I think it's still necessary," said Xavier Emmanuelli, French secretary of state for emergency humanitarian action.
Emmanuelli told France 2 television from Kinshasa that hundreds of thousands of refugees from Rwanda and Burundi were still in dire need in eastern Zaire despite the exodus.

"I think we'd have to think hard before cancelling this force because we had a terrible task getting consensus from the international community" to deploy troops in Zaire, he said. He reiterated that Paris would not act alone in sending troops.
In Madrid, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said Spain was also committed to sending troops.
"Part of this new situation, of this exodus...is an effect of the announcement that this force was already prepared," he said in an interview with Reuters television.
"The operation needs retouching, but in our opinion it should be maintained."

The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said earlier on Monday that half a million Hutu refugees had now crossed back into Rwanda from Zaire. An estimated 1.2 refugees had been at risk after a Tutsi uprising in eastern Zaire.

"The return of the refugees is encouraging news but this crisis has not been resolved. To end it, there must be a global approach, especially with the holding of a conference on the Great Lakes region," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

Rummelhardt said there were still refugees in the region of Bukavu on the south of Lake Kivu and as a result "the force's mission must continue." The UNCHR said it had no reports of any movement by some 500,000 refugees in the Bukavu area.
The refugees, Hutus who fled the arrival in power of a Tutsi-led movement in 1994, began returning last week after Zairean rebels forced Hutu fighters to flee to the hills.
Countries planning to contribute troops to the mission were due to meet in Stuttgart on Thursday to review the force's size and mandate following the refugees' return.
